Answer: E
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple small nodular opacities with a reticulo-nodular pattern predominantly in the upper and mid lung zones, which is the classic radiographic appearance of silicosis. This fits the description of "nodular opacities" better than sarcoidosis (which typically features prominent bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy) or fibrosis (which shows lower zone honeycombing).
